question: In a colon cancer screening program, a 52-year-old patient undergoes a colonoscopy. The entire colon is normal in appearance, except for the finding of a 2 cm pedicled sigmoid polyp that is removed with a diathermy loop. The anatomopathological result indicates that there is carcinoma "in situ" limited to the head of the polyp. He has a thoracoabdominal CT reported as normal. Indicate what would be the correct conduct to follow:

options.opa: Segmental resection of the affected colon.
options.opc: Local resection of the base of the polyp.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Carcinoma in situ" -> "confined to polyp head" -> "no invasion beyond polyp" -> "no lymphatic spread" -> "normal CT scan" -> "low risk of metastasis" -> "periodic endoscopic surveillance" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Carcinoma in situ" -> "confined to polyp head" -> "no invasion beyond polyp" -> "normal CT scan" -> "local resection unnecessary" -> "periodic endoscopic surveillance" -> 90%
CHAIN: "Carcinoma in situ" -> "confined to polyp head" -> "no invasion beyond polyp" -> "normal CT scan" -> "segmental resection excessive" -> "periodic endoscopic surveillance" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Carcinoma in situ" -> "confined to polyp head" -> "no invasion beyond polyp" -> "normal CT scan" -> "sigmoidectomy unnecessary" -> "periodic endoscopic surveillance" -> 90%
analysis: The patient has a carcinoma in situ, which is a non-invasive cancer confined to the epithelium of the polyp. Since the carcinoma is limited to the head of the polyp and has been completely removed, the standard management is periodic endoscopic surveillance to monitor for any new polyps or changes. There is no need for more invasive procedures like segmental resection or sigmoidectomy, as the CT scan is normal and there is no evidence of invasive cancer.
